MAJOR: `memoryAudit.Audit` now spawns an unbounded goroutine per event (`go func(...)`) with no semaphore/worker pool; a burst of /memory ops can fan out unbounded 2s-timeout DB appends and exhaust the PgStore pool, converting audit-store slowness into an availability incident.

The detached audit goroutine is not drained on shutdown (no WaitGroup/handoff), so in-flight security audit records are silently dropped at process exit; combined with best-effort logging this weakens the AC-1 "structured audit" evidence contract under rolling deploys.

`TestRolePostureBypassRejected` delta only asserts `relforcerowsecurity`; the C-8 control also requires NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS for the connecting role, which the test still never checks — a superuser/`rolbypassrls` connection still passes, so the prior bypass-evidence gap is only half-resolved.
MINOR: Audit `Resource` format changes from `recordID` to `projectID + "/" + recordID` with no compatibility note; downstream consumers keying on record ID will break silently (audit schema/join contract change shipped without versioning).
The async path has no test: no coverage that `memory_audit_failures_total` is incremented or that the failure log fires, so the new observability path can regress undetected.

Failure log prints tenant/project/actor/record at `log.Printf` default level on every retry-less failure; consider structured logger/redaction policy consistency with the design's "no secrets" audit rule.
NIT: The goroutine closure duplicates the previously extracted audit context setup inline; a small named helper would keep the fire-and-forget path reusable and testable.
SUMMARY: Delta usefully resolves the two prior MAJORs on synchronous/discarded audit errors and strengthens the FORCE-RLS assertion, but replaces them with unbounded fire-and-forget goroutines and no shutdown drain — audit durability is now probabilistic.
Top risks: audit-path resource exhaustion under load, silent audit loss at shutdown, and C-8 role-posture evidence still not proving NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS.
